goals: Get the signs of u, v and f right

cards.title: The mirror formula
cards.body:
**1/v + 1/u = 1/f**

u is the object distance, v the image distance and f the focal length, all measured from the pole of the mirror.

cards.title: Signs, in one look
cards.remember: Measure every distance from the pole.

cards.question: For a concave mirror, what is the sign of the focal length?
cards.why: The focus of a concave mirror is in front of it, against the direction of the incoming light. So f is negative.

cards.question: An object is 30 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 20 cm. Where is the image?
steps: v = −60 cm: the image is 60 cm in front of the mirror, so it's real

cards.title: Magnification
cards.body:
**m = −v/u** = image height / object height.
- m negative: the image is real and inverted.
- m positive: the image is virtual and erect.
- |m| > 1: larger; |m| < 1: smaller.

cards.question: A mirror gives a magnification of +0.5. What is the image like?
cards.why: A positive m means virtual and erect, and 0.5 is less than 1, so the image is half the size. That's what a convex mirror always gives.

cards.question: For the image found earlier (u = −30 cm, v = −60 cm), find the magnification.
steps: Negative, so real and inverted; 2, so twice as large

cards.question: In the mirror formula, the object distance u is…
cards.why: The object is always placed in front of the mirror, against the direction of the incoming light, so u is always negative.

points: u is always negative; f is negative for concave and positive for convex
m = −v/u: negative means real and inverted
